problem: Mobile pick-and-place methods on OVMM trust noisy open-vocabulary detections (unusual views, occlusion, small objects) and lack a principled way to trade off global frontier exploration against gathering extra views of candidate objects; incorrect detections are a major failure cause.
motivation: Object search needs both long-horizon exploration and short-horizon object verification, which require different representations and objectives. Modeling multi-view consistency of detections lets the robot act only when confident and decide between exploring and re-observing.
key_idea: Build a hierarchical map (2D occupancy + semantic value maps + sparse object-centric 3D Gaussians with Dirichlet class distributions) and plan with a search objective that combines semantic score, expected information gain, and distance to choose between frontiers and re-viewing candidate objects.
insight: Explicit modeling of detection uncertainty helps: on OVMM (1 pick) the trusting baseline gets 13.7 FindObj / 1.3 SR versus 23.8 / 2.5 for the full method, and removing the global objective loses much of the gain (16.8 / 1.7). The optimistic information-gain assumption clearly beats a 50-50 one (unlimited picks FindObj 42.3 vs 26.0). With GT semantics the gain shrinks and SR rises to 21.0, showing detection is the key bottleneck while collisions and placement remain big failures. Object-only 3DGS also uses far less GPU memory than full-scene 3DGS (max avg allocated 4.1 GB vs 8.9 GB).
method: Hierarchical map: 2D BEV occupancy map from depth (frontiers, FMM path planning), 2D semantic value maps (BLIP-2 similarity, VLFM-style, one layer for pick and one for place location), and sparse 3D Gaussians only for task-relevant detected objects

Dirichlet semantic fusion: each Gaussian keeps a categorical distribution over classes updated by Bayesian kernel inference from Detic detections (scaled by alpha_cpa=3); yields class score S and uncertainty U, and object-level uncertainty-weighted score Psi = S - alpha_cs*U

Instance clustering: Gaussians of the same top class are clustered via a 0.5 m voxel grid with 26-connected components; new Gaussians are created by depth error; re-observation masks avoid ignoring negative evidence
Information gain: Dirichlet entropy reduction under an optimistic assumed future observation (all views classify the object as the target class), rendered from candidate gaze poses

Global search objective: V = S*IG - alpha_d*dist for candidate objects and F*F0 - alpha_d*dist for frontiers, with F0 calibrating frontier values against object scores, to choose between exploring and re-viewing

Local search: gaze points on a contour around the object's ground projection (filtered by occupancy/height); all gaze points visited for pick-location search, only the best single view for verification; thresholds tau=0.5 to grasp or place, and views are taken only if the score could rise by at least tau_inc
Modular skills: modified FMM^2 planner with continuous actions and collision checks; oracle pick in sim plus a heuristic drop for placing; Spot API grasp in real world

setting.backbone: Detic detector + BLIP-2 (frozen pretrained VLMs), hand-designed planner; DepthPro for monocular depth on the real robot
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (sim); RGB with DepthPro monocular depth on Spot
setting.action_space: continuous waypoint-based navigation actions (forward 0.1-1.0 m, rotate 5-30 deg) plus pick/place skills
setting.simulator: Habitat (HomeRobot OVMM, HSSD scenes) + real Spot robot
setting.privileged: Oracle pick skill in sim; with more than 1 pick attempt the pick failure reveals GT info; a separate ablation uses GT semantics (not the main result)

numbers.extra: 1 pick attempt; oracle pick skill, heuristic place

numbers_note: Benchmark name mapped to HomeRobot-OVMM (not in the canonical list; original label 'HomeRobot-OVMM'). Hardware results are given only in figures (10 trials x 5 scenarios).
results: On the OVMM val split with 1 pick, HELIOS reaches SR 2.5 versus 1.7 for MoManipVLA and at most 0.6 for the HomeRobot baselines, and is better on all metrics except FindObj, where HomeRobot H/R/R has 29.4. With 5 or unlimited picks it reaches SR 3.1 and 3.2, and it beats the trusting agent in the real Spot experiments.
limitations: Absolute SR stays very low (2.5-3.2%) because of collisions, weak physical placing (dropping objects that roll off), and inefficient search
Class set must be specified at episode start, and gaze-point generation is not information-aware, adding overhead
More than 1 pick attempt uses GT information in the benchmark, and the hardware baseline is only the trusting-agent ablation
builds_on: Wilson et al. (Bayesian kernel semantic Gaussian modeling)
